chapter_plans.title: The Trap
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: Elle Reyes executes the kill plan — but it is a trap; Kroll expected her, and she barely escapes with her life.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Elle Reyes executes the plan: she breaches Kroll's estate during the twelve-minute window, sedates him in his bedroom, and moves to the study to retrieve the dead man's switch. But when she opens the floor safe, she finds not a hard drive but a single photograph: herself, at the riverbank, with the witness. The safe is empty of evidence. Kroll was not sedated — the man in the bed was a decoy. Elle Reyes realizes the trap too late. Alarms blare. She runs through the estate as security closes in, barely escaping through a window into the garden. She hides in a drainage ditch as Kroll's men search the grounds. She escapes, but she is wounded — a deep cut on her arm from the window glass. She returns to her apartment to find a text from Kroll: 'I told you I knew what you were. Now everyone will.'

chapter_plans.one_line_summary: As Elle Reyes scrambles to find the dead man's switch, fragments of her origin wound surface — the night she killed for the first time, and why she started.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: The pressure of the Project Phoenix file triggers a cascade of memories for Elle Reyes. She flashes back to the night of her first kill — not Maya's murderer, but the man who killed her sister, years ago. The reader learns that Elle's origin is not a cold case she stumbled upon, but a personal wound: her sister was murdered, the system failed, and Elle executed the killer herself. She has been doing this for years, not for justice, but for vengeance disguised as justice. The chapter intercuts between the present (Elle searching for the dead man's switch) and the past (the first kill), revealing that her rule — only the guilty — is a lie she tells herself. She killed her sister's murderer, and she has been chasing that feeling ever since. The chapter ends with Elle Reyes, in the present, finding a clue to the dead man's switch location: a storage unit rental receipt in Kroll's name, dated the same week she first contacted him. She dismissed it as a lie, but now, looking at Kroll's file, she realizes the name he mentioned matches a contact in Kroll's phone records. [CLUE C008] As she reviews the Project Phoenix file again, she notices a single photograph is missing from the sequence — the one that would have shown the witness's face. Kroll has redacted it, but the file metadata reveals the witness's name: a woman named 'Elena Vasquez' — the same name that appeared in the watcher's first text to Elle, months ago.

He saw her face and recognized her from the podcast. He has been picked up by Cole's team and is being held as a material witness. Elle Reyes must decide: let the witness talk and risk exposure, or silence him. She chooses a third option: she goes to the witness, not to threaten him, but to tell him the truth. She asks him to tell Cole what he saw — but to leave out her face, claiming he only saw a figure in the dark. The witness agrees, moved by her honesty. Elle Reyes leaves, knowing she has tied off the loose end, but also knowing that her method is changing — she is no longer just a killer; she is becoming something else. The chapter ends with Elle Reyes receiving a text from Mira: 'You're learning. Now finish it.'

chapter_plans.title: The Final Confrontation
chapter_plans.one_line_summary: The final confrontation with Detective Cole — earned through physical evidence, not confession — ends with Kroll's death framed as justice, but Elle's secrecy is shattered.
chapter_plans.beat_summary: Elle Reyes receives a summons from Detective Cole: he has enough circumstantial evidence to bring her in for questioning, but not enough to arrest her. She goes to the station, knowing this is the final confrontation. Cole lays out his case: the timeline, the witness, the riverbank photograph, the Voss recording. He doesn't have a confession, but he has enough to make her life hell. Elle Reyes plays her final card: she reveals the Lucia Vega file — the one she didn't open — and tells Cole that Kroll's own evidence proves his guilt. She offers to hand over the file in exchange for immunity for her network. Cole, a man who believes in the system, hesitates. He knows Kroll was guilty. He knows Elle is a vigilante. But he also knows that putting her away will destroy the only chance Lucia Vega's family has for closure. He makes a choice: he lets Elle walk, but warns her that if she ever kills again, he will find her. The chapter ends with Elle Reyes leaving the station, her thumb tapping her ring finger three times. She is free, but she is no longer invisible. The hunt is over. The cost is counted. And the reader knows: Elle Reyes will never be the same. [CLUE C008] The 'Voss' thread is resolved — Voss is arrested for conspiracy to obstruct justice, based on the evidence Elle planted in chapter 31 (the strand of hair on Kroll's collar). Elle learns of Voss's arrest via a text from Mira during the confrontation, confirming the frame held.
chapter_plans.opens_with: "'Sit down, Elle.' Detective Cole's voice was tired. He gestured to the chair across from him. 'We need to talk about Damien Kroll.' I sat. My thumb started tapping before I could stop it."
chapter_plans.cliffhanger: Elle Reyes walks out of the station into the cold night air. She is free, but she is no longer invisible. Her phone buzzes. A text from Mira: 'You did it. Now what?' Elle types back: 'Now I disappear. For real this time.' She looks up at the sky, takes a breath, and walks into the darkness. The hunt is over. But the quiet ones are never truly gone.
